rules.reason: an attestation only its submitter can look up is not an attestation, it is a favour -- the entire value of lodging a digest with an independent party is that a third person (a customer, an auditor, the other side of an argument) can check it without an account here, a relationship with the operator, or anybody's permission. The page reads nothing keyed to a person and returns nothing but a hex string, a timestamp and the submitter's own chosen label

PUBLIC on the object, GATED IN THE OBJECT: action_notarize refuses an anonymous submission with a 409 naming notary.public_submission unless the operator has set it. The gate lives in the code rather than here because the two deployments are one setting apart -- a notary run as a service for other people must accept strangers, a notary run for one business's own ledger heads must not -- and an operator should not have to edit permission rules to change which one they are running. Accepting a digest is close to the safest write on this box in any case: it stores 64 hex characters, learns nothing about the submitter, and cannot overwrite or move an existing record

READ ONLY, and read only is the entire product. No update and no delete are granted here because a notary with an edit path is a notary whose operator can be leaned on, and every claim anybody makes from this log rests on there being no way to amend it after the fact. No create either: action_notarize is the one writer, because a row typed by hand is a timestamp somebody chose rather than one the server observed, and the object is also what enforces that resubmitting returns the ORIGINAL record instead of a later one. The collection is append storage besides, so there is no update or delete to grant even if somebody wanted to
